explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/68: 'Weisenberg has observed that this sum can also be written as Σ_{k≥1} Σ_{n≥2} 1/(n!)^k.' The Lean statement proves Σ' n, 1/((n+2)! − 1) = Σ' n, Σ' k, 1/((n+2)!)^{k+1}, i.e. the same double sum with the order of summation n outside, k inside (equal to the page's order since all terms are positive). It follows termwise from the geometric series and is proved in the file. Correct.
